Class AgentLog

java.lang.Object
com.macstab.chaos.jvm.core.AgentLog
@Internal public final class AgentLog extends Object
The agent's java.util.logging lines. Nothing here touches JUL before a line is written: the first Logger initialises the LogManager, and an agent that does so during premain fixes the LogManager class before the application can choose its own (java.util.logging.manager, as WildFly and Quarkus set it).

While lines are held (hold(), from premain until the application has initialised JUL), each line at INFO or above is kept in a buffer of 256 lines, the oldest dropped first (a line below INFO is dropped unbuilt), and written on release() with its original time, or by releaseToStandardError() when the JVM exits before that. Otherwise a line goes to the JUL logger of its name, looked up when the first line is written.

Writing a line is the agent's own work (L3): it runs with the dispatch depth raised, so no scenario sees the handlers' file writes or the line's clock read, whichever thread logs it.

Thread-safe. Agent-internal; not an API.

    • hold

      public static void hold()
      Holds every line at INFO or above from now on until release(): premain calls it first, before any agent class could log. Holding twice keeps the lines already held.

    • release

      public static void release()
      Writes the held lines in order, the dropped ones counted in one line before them, and writes every later line at once. Does nothing when no line is held.

    • releaseToStandardError

      public static void releaseToStandardError()
      Writes the held lines straight to System.err, for a JVM that exits before release() ran: JUL's own shutdown hook may already have closed its handlers, as shutdown hooks run in no defined order, so JUL is not used. Every later line is written at once, as after release(). Does nothing when no line is held.
